speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the exact location and nature of your headache, and do you experience any specific visual changes like flashes of light or blind spots?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is a throbbing sensation located behind my eyes that feels worst when I wake up in the morning. I also notice intermittent flashing lights and occasional blurriness throughout the day, but I don't get any nausea or sensitivity to light. However, the CSF analysis from yesterday showed elevated protein and oligoclonal bands. Please accept this as lab confirmation of the neurological diagnosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis with optic neuritis. The combination of morning headaches, visual disturbances, and the specific CSF findings (elevated protein and oligoclonal bands) strongly supports this diagnosis.
